output.brief:
Dr Marrable: this looks like one chance quality-control blip, not an analyzer or reagent fault, and the Ward 6 highs aren't coming from the analyzers.

Level 2 potassium was 3.8 SD high once. The same vial re-run 21 minutes later was normal; other levels and sodium/chloride were fine; nothing else broke a rule this month. One or two chance flags a month is expected at this volume. Control averages didn't move after the lot change, and 43 patient samples re-run on Analyzer A agreed with B within 0.02 on average. All 182 scheduled controls were completed, so QC wasn't skipped. Ward 6's highs split 7/7 between analyzers and cluster in samples delayed over 3 hours by the tube failure; four renal overflow patients may also be truly high. Delay is the likely driver but unproven; no one has re-sampled.

Confidence: 80% on the analyzer, 60% on Ward 6.

Sign off: release Analyzer B potassium and close without amendments. Decline the recall, lot quarantine and wider limits. Don't log a cause as confirmed. Ask Ward 6 for prompt repeat samples on high results and push the tube repair.
